'''Esteban José Jean-Pierre Ocon-Khelfane''' ({{IPA|fr|ɛs.te.ban ɔ.kɔ̃}}; born 17 September 1996) is a French [[racing driver]] who most recently competed in [[Formula One]] for [[Haas F1 Team|Haas]]. Ocon won the [[2021 Hungarian Grand Prix]] with [[Alpine F1 Team|Alpine]].

Born and raised in [[Normandy]] to a [[working-class]] family, Ocon began competitive [[kart racing]] aged nine, winning several national and international titles. Graduating to [[junior formulae]] in 2012, Ocon won his first title at the [[2014 FIA Formula 3 European Championship]] with [[Prema Racing|Prema]], ahead of [[Tom Blomqvist]] and [[Max Verstappen]]. Ocon then won the [[2015 GP3 Series]] with [[ART Grand Prix|ART]], achieving 14 podiums in 18 races. A member of the [[Mercedes Junior Team]] since 2015, Ocon made his Formula One debut at the [[2016 Belgian Grand Prix]] with [[Manor Racing|Manor]], replacing [[Rio Haryanto]]  for the remainder of the {{F1|2016}} season. He moved to [[Force India]]—who later became [[Racing Point Force India|Racing Point]]—in {{F1|2017}}, partnering [[Sergio Pérez]]. Ocon left Racing Point at the end of {{F1|2018}}, becoming a reserve driver for [[Mercedes-Benz in Formula One|Mercedes]] in {{F1|2019}}.

Ocon returned as a full-time driver with [[Renault in Formula One|Renault]] in {{F1|2020}}, taking his maiden podium finish at the {{F1GP|2020|Sakhir}}. Retaining his seat for {{F1|2021}}, Ocon partnered [[Fernando Alonso]] at the re-branded [[Alpine F1 Team|Alpine]], taking his maiden [[List of Formula One Grand Prix winners|victory]] at the [[2021 Hungarian Grand Prix|Hungarian Grand Prix]]. After a less successful {{F1|2022}} campaign, during which he became the first teammate to outscore Alonso in the championship since [[Jenson Button]] in {{F1|2015}}, Ocon achieved his third podium at the [[2023 Monaco Grand Prix]]. In {{F1|2024}}—his final season at Alpine—Ocon achieved his maiden [[List of Formula One drivers who set a fastest lap|fastest lap]] in the [[2024 United States Grand Prix|United States]], followed by a fourth career podium at the rain-affected {{F1GP|2024|São Paulo}}. He left Alpine after the {{F1GP|2024|Qatar}}, moving to [[Haas F1 Team|Haas]] for {{F1|2025}} alongside [[Oliver Bearman]], prior to another early departure in {{F1|2026}}. Ocon achieved {{Numbertoword|{{F1stat|OCO|wins}}}} race win, {{Numbertoword|{{F1stat|OCO|fastestlaps}}}} fastest lap and {{Numbertoword|{{F1stat|OCO|podiums}}}} podiums in Formula One.

== Early and personal life ==
Esteban José Jean-Pierre Ocon-Khelfane was born on 17 September 1996 in [[Évreux]], [[Normandy]] to Sabrina Khelfane and Laurent Ocon, a mechanic who owns a garage in Évreux.<ref name="FN">{{cite web |author1=Petr Kubala |title=Carl, José, Maria, Joseph. Znáte celá jména jezdců formule 1? |url=https://f1sport.auto.cz/clanek/cela-jmena-jezdcu-f1#part=3 |website=F1sport.cz |access-date=25 April 2021 |language=cs |archive-date=25 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210425123122/https://f1sport.auto.cz/clanek/cela-jmena-jezdcu-f1#part=3 |url-status=live }}</ref> His paternal family is originally from [[Málaga]], Spain, and his mother has roots in Algeria.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://lemag.seinesaintdenis.fr/Esteban-Ocon-la-vie-en-pole|title=Esteban Ocon, la vie en pole|website=Seine-Saint-Denis – Le magazine|access-date=27 April 2017|archive-date=28 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170428054232/http://lemag.seinesaintdenis.fr/Esteban-Ocon-la-vie-en-pole|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.planetf1.com/driver/esteban-ocon/biography|title=Esteban Ocon Biography|website=PlanetF1}}</ref> While competing in karting, his parents decided to sell their family home, which included his father's garage, to fund his karting career. After selling the house, they lived and travelled to races in a caravan Ocon also used as a motor home.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Richards|first=Giles|date=27 August 2021|title=Esteban Ocon: I didn't have the right to fail, I had to succeed|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2021/aug/27/esteban-ocon-formula-one-i-didnt-have-the-right-to-fail-i-had-to-succeed|url-status=live|access-date=22 October 2021|website=[[The Guardian]]|archive-date=22 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211022204814/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2021/aug/27/esteban-ocon-formula-one-i-didnt-have-the-right-to-fail-i-had-to-succeed}}</ref> Ocon admitted that he almost gave up on his racing career to work at [[McDonald's]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/i-nearly-went-to-work-in-mcdonalds-admits-f1s-rising-star-esteban-ocon-3vl652w0f |title=I nearly went to work in McDonald's, admits F1's rising star Esteban Ocon |first=Rebecca |last=Clancy |date=15 July 2017 |access-date=12 December 2024 |work=[[The Times]] |publisher=[[News UK]] |issn=0140-0460}}</ref>

{{As of|2022}}, Ocon lives in [[Geneva]], Switzerland. Besides his native French language, Ocon also speaks English, Spanish and Italian. In 2023 Ocon began a relationship with  model, social media influencer, medical student and former [[Miss Côte d'Azur]] Flavy Barla having split with his previous girlfriend Elena Berri (whom he had started dating in 2018) earlier in 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/f1-news-alpine-news-who-is-flavy-barla-esteban-ocons-new-girlfriend-after-his-breakup-with-elena-berri/ | title=Who is Flavy Barla? – Esteban Ocon's New Girlfriend After His Breakup with Elena Berri | date=30 December 2023 }}</ref>

== Junior racing career ==
=== Karting (2006–2011) ===
Ocon entered [[karting]] in 2006, when he finished eighth in the Minime class of the French Championship.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.driverdb.com/standings/1247-2006/|title=Championnat de France – Minime 2006|work=driverdb.com|publisher=Driver Database|access-date=18 October 2013|archive-date=19 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019170635/http://www.driverdb.com/standings/1247-2006/|url-status=live}}</ref> He won the championship in 2007 and continued his success by winning the Cadet class in 2008 ahead of [[Anthoine Hubert]] and [[Pierre Gasly]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.driverdb.com/standings/1247-2007/|title=Championnat de France – Minime 2007|work=driverdb.com|publisher=Driver Database|access-date=18 October 2013|archive-date=19 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019170631/http://www.driverdb.com/standings/1247-2007/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.driverdb.com/standings/2456-2008/|title=Championnat de France – Cadet 2008|work=driverdb.com|publisher=Driver Database|access-date=18 October 2013|archive-date=19 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019170628/http://www.driverdb.com/standings/2456-2008/|url-status=live}}</ref> He then spent three years racing in the [[KF3]] category and competed in the [[Spanish Karting Championship|Spanish Championship]] and [[Italian Open Masters]]. He won the French KF3 title in 2010 and finished as runner-up in the [[WSK Euro Series]] in 2011 behind [[Max Verstappen]].<ref name="One">{{cite news|url=http://www.paddockscout.com/lotuss-one-to-watch-esteban-ocon/|title=Lotus's one to watch: Esteban Ocon|last=Musker|first=Ant|date=4 October 2013|publisher=Paddock Scout|access-date=18 October 2013|archive-date=20 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020064837/https://www.paddockscout.com/lotuss-one-to-watch-esteban-ocon|url-status=live}}</ref> At the age of 14, Ocon was signed by Gravity Sports management, a sister company of [[Renault in Formula One|Renault F1]] team.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/february-2015/93/esteban-ocon|title=Esteban Ocon|date=9 July 2015|work=Motor Sport Magazine|access-date=27 April 2017|language=en|archive-date=28 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170428053018/http://www.motorsportmagazine.com/archive/article/february-2015/93/esteban-ocon|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Formula Renault 2.0 (2012–2013) ===
==== 2012: Junior formulae debut ====
In 2012, Ocon made his debut in [[Open-wheel car|single-seaters]], taking part in the [[2012 Eurocup Formula Renault 2.0|Eurocup Formula Renault 2.0]] with [[Koiranen GP|Koiranen Motorsport]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.italiaracing.net/notizia.asp?id=34122&cat=22|title=Ocon e Pakari pronti per il debutto|date=13 December 2011|trans-title=Ocon and Pacari ready for debut|work=ItaliaRacing.net|publisher=Inpagina|language=it|access-date=13 December 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120601115038/http://www.italiaracing.net/notizia.asp?id=34122&cat=22|archive-date=1 June 2012}}</ref> He finished fourteenth with four point-scoring finishes, including being on the podium at his home round at [[Circuit Paul Ricard]].<ref name="One"/> He also contested a partial campaign in the [[2012 Formula Renault 2.0 Alps Series|Formula Renault 2.0 Alps]] with Koiranen,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.renaultsportitalia.it/art/news_20120131_alps_eng.html|title=F.Renault 2.0 ALPS synonimous (sic) of quality with top team and drivers ready to roll in 2012 season|date=8 March 2012|work=Renaultsport Italia|publisher=Fast Lane Promotion|access-date=8 March 2012|archive-date=28 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128024024/http://www.renaultsportitalia.it/art/news_20120131_alps_eng.html|url-status=live}}</ref> finishing seventh with two podiums, both of which came at the [[Red Bull Ring]].

==== 2013: Maiden victories in the Eurocup and Northern European Cup ====
Ocon remained in the series for [[2013 Eurocup Formula Renault 2.0|2013]], switching to the [[R-ace GP|ART Junior Team]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gpupdate.net/en/f1-news/290630/lotus-f1-junior-team-drivers-announced/|title=Lotus F1 Junior Team drivers announced|date=15 February 2013|work=GPUpdate.net|publisher=JHED Media BV|access-date=15 February 2013|archive-date=1 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201131748/https://www.gpupdate.net/en/f1-news/290630/lotus-f1-junior-team-drivers-announced/|url-status=live}}</ref> He recorded one [[pole position]] and won two races including at Circuit Paul Ricard, finishing the season in third place behind Pierre Gasly and [[Oliver Rowland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.paddockscout.com/ocon-takes-first-eurocup-victory-in-frantic-race-two/|title=Ocon takes first Eurocup victory in frantic race two|last=Musker|first=Ant|date=29 September 2013|publisher=Paddock Scout|access-date=18 October 2013|archive-date=20 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020064825/https://www.paddockscout.com/ocon-takes-first-eurocup-victory-in-frantic-race-two|url-status=live}}</ref> A partial campaign in the [[2013 Formula Renault 2.0 Northern European Cup|Northern European Cup]] produced a race win at the [[Hockenheimring]] and two further podiums.

=== Formula Three (2013–2014) ===
==== 2013: F3 debut at Macau ====
[[File:2014 F3 HockenheimringII Esteban Ocon by 2eight 8SC1548.jpg|thumb|Esteban Ocon in F3 – Hockenheimring 2014]]
Ocon made his debut in [[Formula Three]] machinery at the [[2013 Macau Grand Prix]] with [[Prema Powerteam]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/110665|title=Lotus Formula 1 protege Esteban Ocon gets Prema Macau Formula 3 seat|last=Simmons|first=Marcus|date=15 October 2013|work=[[Autosport]]|publisher=[[Haymarket Media Group|Haymarket Publications]]|access-date=18 October 2013|archive-date=16 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016000326/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/110665|url-status=live}}</ref> He stalled at the start of the main race but went on to finish tenth.

==== 2014: Maiden title in FIA European F3 ====
[[File:2014 F3 HockenheimringII Esteban Ocon by 2eight DSC7632.jpg|left|thumb|Ocon on the podium at the 2014 F3 European Hockenheimring round]]
Ocon continued his collaboration with Prema into the [[2014 FIA Formula 3 European Championship]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.formularapida.net/news/exclusive-esteban-ocon-in-f3-with-prema-powerteam-for-2014/|title=Esteban Ocon in F3 with Prema Powerteam for 2014|last=Vendrell|first=Arnau Viñals|date=19 October 2013|publisher=formularapida.net|access-date=20 October 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022201528/http://www.formularapida.net/news/exclusive-esteban-ocon-in-f3-with-prema-powerteam-for-2014/|archive-date=22 October 2013}}</ref> He topped the standings at the first round at [[Silverstone Circuit]] and remained in the lead of the championship for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.paddockscout.com/verstappen-claims-ninth-win-as-ocon-is-crowned-champion/|title=Verstappen claims ninth win as Ocon is crowned champion|last=Khorounzhiy|first=Valentin|date=18 October 2014|publisher=Paddock Scout|access-date=18 October 2014|archive-date=20 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020051612/https://www.paddockscout.com/verstappen-claims-ninth-win-as-ocon-is-crowned-champion|url-status=live}}</ref> With two rounds to spare, he made a brief appearance in the [[2014 Formula Renault 3.5 Series]] with [[Comtec Racing]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/115774|title=Lotus F1 junior, European F3 leader Esteban Ocon makes FR3.5 debut|last=Simmons|first=Marcus|work=[[Autosport]]|publisher=[[Haymarket Media Group|Haymarket Publications]]|date=8 September 2014|access-date=19 October 2014|archive-date=27 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160827091131/http://www.autosport.com/news/report.php/id/115774|url-status=live}}</ref> Ocon was crowned FIA Formula 3 European champion with three races remaining, ahead of [[Tom Blomqvist]] and [[Max Verstappen]]. He finished on the podium in twenty-one of the thirty-three races, winning nine, and recorded fifteen pole positions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/formula-european-masters/news/ocon-claims-title-verstappen-wins-race-at-imola/457500/|date=13 October 2014|title=Ocon claims title, Verstappen wins race at Imola|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Motorsport.com]]|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529100738/https://www.motorsport.com/formula-european-masters/news/ocon-claims-title-verstappen-wins-race-at-imola/457500/|url-status=live}}</ref> Ocon made a second appearance at the [[2014 Macau Grand Prix|Macau Grand Prix in 2014]]. He qualified fourth for the main race but was eliminated by a multi-car collision on the first lap.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f3/news/rosenqvist-victorious-at-macau-458828/458828/|date=14 November 2014|title=Rosenqvist victorious at Macau|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Motorsport.com]]|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529100748/https://www.motorsport.com/f3/news/rosenqvist-victorious-at-macau-458828/458828/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== GP3 Series (2015) ===
Ocon moved to the [[GP3 Series]] for [[2015 GP3 Series|2015]] with [[ART Grand Prix]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Simmons|first=Marcus|url=https://www.autosport.com/fia-f3/news/esteban-ocon-completes-move-into-gp3-with-art-5009908/5009908/|date=11 March 2015|title=Esteban Ocon completes move into GP3 with ART|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Autosport.com]]|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529100735/https://www.autosport.com/fia-f3/news/esteban-ocon-completes-move-into-gp3-with-art-5009908/5009908/|url-status=live}}</ref> Despite only scoring one race victory (two other victories were denied due to penalties),<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bradley|first=Charkes|url=https://www.motorsport.com/fia-f3/news/barcelona-gp3-ocon-dominates-season-opener/568105/|date=9 May 2015|title=Barcelona GP3: Ocon dominates season opener|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Motorsport.com]]|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529100748/https://www.motorsport.com/fia-f3/news/barcelona-gp3-ocon-dominates-season-opener/568105/|url-status=live}}</ref> he won the championship by eight points ahead of [[Luca Ghiotto]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Khorounzhiy|first=Valentin|url=https://www.motorsport.com/fia-f3/news/abu-dhabi-gp3-ocon-crowned-champion-as-palou-takes-maiden-win/660598/|date=29 November 2015|title=Abu Dhabi GP3: Ocon crowned champion as Palou takes maiden win|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Motorsport.com]]|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529100735/https://www.motorsport.com/fia-f3/news/abu-dhabi-gp3-ocon-crowned-champion-as-palou-takes-maiden-win/660598/|url-status=live}}</ref> Ocon recorded three pole positions and fourteen podium finishes (including nine consecutive second-places) from eighteen races.

=== DTM (2016) ===
Ocon drove for [[Mercedes-Benz in motorsport|Mercedes-Benz]] in the first ten races of the [[2016 Deutsche Tourenwagen Masters|2016 DTM season]], alongside his Formula One reserve driver role at [[Renault in Formula One|Renault]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=on poised for Renault reserve role|date=2 February 2016|url=https://f1i.com/news/40315-ocon-poised-for-renault-reserve-role.html|access-date=29 May 2023|language=en|archive-date=1 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230701110842/https://f1i.com/news/40315-ocon-poised-for-renault-reserve-role.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Elizalde|first=Pablo|url=https://www.motorsport.com/dtm/news/mercedes-confirms-ocon-s-dtm-move-672766/672766/|date=11 February 2016|title=Mercedes confirms Ocon's DTM move|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Motorsport.com]]|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529100735/https://www.motorsport.com/dtm/news/mercedes-confirms-ocon-s-dtm-move-672766/672766/|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored two points finishing ninth in the first race at [[Circuit Zandvoort]], before he was promoted to a Formula 1 race seat. He was replaced by [[Felix Rosenqvist]] following his promotion.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Khorounzhiy|first=Valentin|url=https://www.motorsport.com/dtm/news/rosenqvist-to-replace-ocon-for-dtm-round-in-moscow-806322/806322/|date=10 August 2016|title=Rosenqvist to replace Ocon for DTM round in Moscow|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Motorsport.com]]|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529100740/https://www.motorsport.com/dtm/news/rosenqvist-to-replace-ocon-for-dtm-round-in-moscow-806322/806322/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Formula One career ==
=== Test driver (2014–2016) ===
[[File:Esteban Ocon - Mercedes (32729175350).jpg|thumb|Ocon driving the [[Mercedes F1 W07 Hybrid]]|left]]
Ocon was signed to [[Lotus F1 Team]]'s driver development programme in 2010 whilst he was competing in karting.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.haasf1team.com/season/team/esteban-ocon|title=Esteban Ocon|website=haasf1team.com|accessdate=27 September 2026}}</ref> In October 2014, as a reward for winning the FIA Formula 3 European Championship, Lotus gave him his first experience of a Formula One car; he completed a two-day test at [[Circuit Ricardo Tormo]], driving the 2012 [[Lotus E20]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/esteban-ocon-completes-lotus-f1-test/457880/|title=Esteban Ocon completes Lotus F1 test|website=motorsport.com|date=23 October 2014|access-date=6 January 2020|archive-date=10 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210030815/https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/esteban-ocon-completes-lotus-f1-test/457880/|url-status=live}}</ref> A week later, he completed another test as a prize for his championship victory, driving the 2010 [[Ferrari F10]] at [[Fiorano Circuit]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/headlines/2014/10/Ferrari-impressed-by-Ocon-after-Fiorano-test.html|title=Ferrari impressed by Ocon after Fiorano test|website=formula1.com|date=30 October 2014|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=7 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230807074922/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/headlines/2014/10/Ferrari-impressed-by-Ocon-after-Fiorano-test.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In November, Ocon made his Grand Prix weekend debut for Lotus during the first practice (FP1) session at the [[2014 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix|Abu Dhabi Grand Prix]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2014/races/916/abu-dhabi/practice-1.html|title=2014 Formula 1 Etihad Airways Abu Dhabi Grand Prix – Practice 1|website=formula1.com|date=21 November 2014|access-date=6 January 2020|archive-date=22 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190622154701/https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2014/races/916/abu-dhabi/practice-1.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In May 2015, Ocon entered into an agreement with [[Mercedes in F1|Mercedes]]; he would receive the team's support for his upcoming GP3 Series campaign and would also serve as Mercedes' test and reserve driver in the DTM championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.racefans.net/2015/05/07/ocon-joins-mercedes-young-driver-roster/|title=Ocon joins Mercedes' young driver roster|website=RaceFans|last=Collantine|first=Keith|date=7 May 2015|access-date=6 September 2024}}</ref> Mercedes team principal [[Toto Wolff]] described Ocon as "mega-talented" and commented that the team would be "watching [his] progress with a lot of interest".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/dtm/news/mega-talented-ocon-gains-mercedes-support-and-gp3-drive/3222293/|title='Mega-talented' Ocon gains Mercedes support and GP3 drive|website=motorsport.com|date=8 May 2015|accessdate=27 September 2026}}</ref> Shortly afterwards, Ocon was called up by [[Force India]] to drive the [[Force India VJM08|VJM08]] at the in-season test at the [[Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya]] after [[Pascal Wehrlein]] was forced to withdraw due to illness.<ref>{{cite === Mercedes reserve driver (2019) ===
After Force India changed ownership in 2018, it was revealed that Ocon had an "informal agreement" to join Renault for {{F1|2019}}.<ref name="crash.net">{{Cite web |title=Why Mercedes could lose out f1 silly season |date=20 August 2018 |url=https://www.crash.net/f1/feature/903525/1/why-mercedes-could-lose-out-f1-s-silly-season }}</ref> Renault instead unexpectedly signed Daniel Ricciardo, leaving Ocon's future in doubt and attracting criticism from Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff.<ref name="crash.net"/><ref name="BBC Wolff">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/45522631|title=Singapore GP: Toto Wolff criticises Renault over Esteban Ocon U-turn|website=bbc.co.uk|date=14 September 2018|access-date=6 January 2020|archive-date=13 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200713094846/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/45522631|url-status=live}}</ref> Ocon's seat at Force India (now [[Racing Point]]) was taken by Lance Stroll. Other teams were said to have been reluctant to hire a Mercedes-contracted driver, but Wolff was unwilling to release Ocon, predicting that "one day he is going to be in a Mercedes and win races and championships".<ref name="BBC Wolff"/>

Left without a race seat for 2019, Ocon and his management decided against racing in a different series and he was instead placed in a reserve driver role with Mercedes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/ocon-chance-race-outside-2019/3210280/|title=Ocon turned down chance to race outside F1 in 2019|website=motorsport.com|date=9 November 2018|accessdate=28 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Noble |first1=Jonathan |last2=Beer |first2=Matt |title=Esteban Ocon gets 2019 Mercedes F1 reserve driver role |url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/140281/ocon-gets-mercedes-reserve-role-for-2019 |website=autosport.com |access-date=30 November 2018 |date=23 November 2018 |archive-date=30 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181130202005/https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/140281/ocon-gets-mercedes-reserve-role-for-2019 |url-status=live }}</ref> He performed simulator work for the team and drove the [[Mercedes AMG F1 W10 EQ Power+|W10]] in two [[Pirelli]] tyre tests.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/esteban-ocon-the-mercedes-man-waiting-in-the-wings.4wKYbSEZeOpRvlMVt1KrIY|title=Esteban Ocon: the Mercedes man waiting in the wings|website=formula1.com|date=22 August 2019|accessdate=28 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/pirelli-completes-first-18-inch-tyre-test/4540921/|title=Pirelli completes first 18-inch tyre test|website=motorsport.com|date=17 September 2019|accessdate=28 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autohebdof1.com/short/f1/Ocon-completes-Pirelli-tests-in-Barcelona-206554.html|title=Ocon completes Pirelli testing in Barcelona|website=autohebdof1.com|date=8 October 2019|accessdate=28 September 2026}}</ref> He claimed to have been in discussions with Mercedes for the {{F1|2020}} season, remarking that he was "very close" to replacing [[Valtteri Bottas]] at the team. Mercedes ultimately decided to continue with Bottas.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.planetf1.com/news/ocon-was-close-to-mercedes/|title=Ocon was 'very close' to 2020 Mercedes seat|website=planetf1.com|date=21 January 2020|access-date=14 March 2021|archive-date=17 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210617232947/https://www.planetf1.com/news/ocon-was-close-to-mercedes/|url-status=live}}</ref>

he finished eleventh after taking new [[Formula One engines|power unit]] elements and starting from the pit lane.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Esteban Just Misses Out On Points at COTA Despite Pitlane Start|date=23 October 2022|url=https://www.esteban-ocon.com/news/esteban-just-misses-out-on-points-at-cota-despite-pitlane-start|access-date=29 May 2023|website=esteban-ocon.com|language=en|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529092442/https://www.esteban-ocon.com/news/esteban-just-misses-out-on-points-at-cota-despite-pitlane-start|url-status=live}}</ref> He was involved in separate collisions with teammate Alonso in the {{F1 GP|2022|São Paulo}} sprint, with the damage to his car dropping him to seventeenth place.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Noble|first=Jonathan|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/f1-ocon-alonso-unaware-clash-teammate-brazil-sprint/10398978/|date=13 November 2022|title=Ocon unaware of second clash with F1 teammate Alonso in Brazil sprint|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Motorsport.com]]|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529092440/https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/f1-ocon-alonso-unaware-clash-teammate-brazil-sprint/10398978/|url-status=live}}</ref> He recovered to score points in the race.<ref>{{Cite web|title='I think we did everything perfect' – Ocon thrilled after comeback drive helps Alpine extend lead over McLaren|date=15 November 2022|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.i-think-we-did-everything-perfect-ocon-thrilled-after-comeback-drive-helps.3uazlqucgDszzYKgx7C2CE.html|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Formula 1]]|language=en|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529111709/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.i-think-we-did-everything-perfect-ocon-thrilled-after-comeback-drive-helps.3uazlqucgDszzYKgx7C2CE.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Ocon ended the season eighth in the drivers' championship, equalling his best result previously achieved in 2017. He scored 92 points to Alonso's 81 but was outqualified by Alonso in twelve out of twenty-two races.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2022 Driver Standings|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2022/drivers.html|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Formula 1]]|language=en|archive-date=12 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220412090734/https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2022/drivers.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/head-to-head-which-drivers-came-out-on-top-in-the-battle-of-the-2022-team.2oAjm6rU67rnQWpNLkvGH8|title=Head-to-head: Which drivers came out on top in the battle of the 2022 team mates?|date=16 December 2022|accessdate=29 September 2026}}</ref> Matt Morlidge at ''[[Sky Sports]]'' described the season as Ocon's "best-ever" but put his points advantage over Alonso down to better car reliability.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12754411/formula-1-driver-ratings-ranking-all-2022-drivers-with-max-verstappen-and-george-russell-the-stars|title=Formula 1 driver ratings: Ranking all 2022 drivers, with Max Verstappen and George Russell the stars|website=skysports.com|date=26 November 2022|accessdate=29 September 2026}}</ref>

==== 2023 season ====
[[File:FIA F1 Austria 2023 Nr. 31 (1).jpg|thumb|Ocon at the [[2023 Austrian Grand Prix]]]]
For {{F1|2023}}, Ocon gained a new teammate in former karting rival Pierre Gasly as Alonso departed to [[Aston Martin in F1|Aston Martin]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Smith|first=Luke|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/fernando-alonso-switches-to-aston-martin-f1-team-from-2023/10347079/|date=1 August 2022|title=Fernando Alonso switches to Aston Martin F1 team from 2023|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Motorsport.com]]|archive-date=24 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221224065745/https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/fernando-alonso-switches-to-aston-martin-f1-team-from-2023/10347079/|url-status=live}}</ref> His training was impacted prior to the start of the season when he got "very sick" with a lung virus.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Smith|first=Luke|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/ocon-got-very-sick-in-f1-off-season-due-to-bad-lung-virus/10433258/|date=17 February 2023|title=Ocon got "very sick" in F1 off-season due to bad lung virus|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Motorsport.com]]|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529094200/https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/ocon-got-very-sick-in-f1-off-season-due-to-bad-lung-virus/10433258/|url-status=live}}</ref>

At the season-opening {{F1 GP|2023|Bahrain}}, Ocon received penalties for being out of position on the grid, failing to serve the penalty correctly and for speeding in the pit lane. He eventually retired from the race with mechanical issues.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.everything-went-wrong-today-says-ocon-after-being-penalised-three-times-and.1Obkye7mOTceYVpzCX9Bp6.html|title='Everything went wrong today' says frustrated Ocon after being penalised three times and retiring early in Bahrain|work=[[Formula 1]]|date=6 March 2023|access-date=6 March 2023|archive-date=6 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306022140/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.everything-went-wrong-today-says-ocon-after-being-penalised-three-times-and.1Obkye7mOTceYVpzCX9Bp6.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12473/12826969/bahrain-grand-prix-esteban-ocon-equals-unwanted-record-with-three-driving-penalties-before-retiring|title=Bahrain Grand Prix: Esteban Ocon equals unwanted record with three driving penalties before retiring|work=Sky Sports|date=5 March 2023|access-date=6 March 2023|archive-date=6 March 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306010744/https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12473/12826969/bahrain-grand-prix-esteban-ocon-equals-unwanted-record-with-three-driving-penalties-before-retiring|url-status=live}}</ref> He started sixth and scored his first points of the season at the {{F1 GP|2023|Saudi Arabian}}, finishing eighth. Running in tenth place at the final restart of the {{F1 GP|2023|Australian}}, Ocon was involved in a heavy collision with teammate Gasly, who apologised for his role in the incident. Ocon crashed in qualifying at the {{F1 GP|2023|Azerbaijan}} and started the race from the pit lane.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ocon to start Azerbaijan Sprint and Grand Prix from pit lane after Alpine make parc ferme changes|date=29 April 2023|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.ocon-to-start-azerbaijan-sprint-and-grand-prix-from-pit-lane-after-alpine.5SEXnfuFG1TAbaCEqJOssg.html|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Formula 1]]|language=en|archive-date=5 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230505113954/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.ocon-to-start-azerbaijan-sprint-and-grand-prix-from-pit-lane-after-alpine.5SEXnfuFG1TAbaCEqJOssg.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Learning the key as BWT Alpine F1 Team look to finish Baku weekend with points|date=29 April 2023|url=https://www.alpine-cars.co.uk/formula-1/f1-news/sprint-azerbaijan-baku-2023.html|access-date=29 May 2023|website=alpinecars.co.uk|language=en|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529094157/https://www.alpine-cars.co.uk/formula-1/f1-news/sprint-azerbaijan-baku-2023.html|url-status=live}}</ref> During the race, Ocon ran on hard tyres until the last lap. Photographers began to enter the pit lane, not realising Ocon was yet to pit, and narrowly avoided being hit by his car.<ref>{{Cite web|title='Absolute shambles': Esteban Ocon almost drives into F1 photographers in near-disaster|date=30 April 2023|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/f1/f1-esteban-ocon-photographers-azerbaijan-baku-b2329771.html|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[The Independent]]|language=en|archive-date=25 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230525085237/https://www.independent.co.uk/f1/f1-esteban-ocon-photographers-azerbaijan-baku-b2329771.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Gasly keen to move on from 'very bad' weekend as Alpine fail to score in Baku|date=2 May 2022|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.gasly-keen-to-move-on-from-very-bad-weekend-as-alpine-fail-to-score-in-baku.7i0fL4Ha0yNXRoj0Pr3Fn2.html|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Formula 1]]|language=en|archive-date=29 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529123237/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.gasly-keen-to-move-on-from-very-bad-weekend-as-alpine-fail-to-score-in-baku.7i0fL4Ha0yNXRoj0Pr3Fn2.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Ocon started third at the {{F1 GP|2023|Monaco}} after [[Charles Leclerc]] ahead received a penalty.<ref>{{Cite web|title='It's a hell of a moment for everyone' says 'very pleased' Ocon after qualifying in P4 for Monaco GP|date=27 May 2023|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.its-a-hell-of-a-moment-for-everyone-says-very-pleased-ocon-after-qualifying.7MnG76wkVKXdS17PmEib4W.html|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Formula 1]]|language=en|archive-date=28 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528121343/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.its-a-hell-of-a-moment-for-everyone-says-very-pleased-ocon-after-qualifying.7MnG76wkVKXdS17PmEib4W.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Ocon held off Carlos Sainz Jr. in the first half of the race but lost a place to George Russell during the pit stops. A mistake and a penalty for Russell allowed Ocon back into third place, earning him his third career podium and the ''Driver Of The Day'' award.<ref>{{Cite web|title=DRIVER OF THE DAY: Ocon gets your vote for mighty drive to P3 in Monaco|date=28 May 2023|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.driver-of-the-day-ocon-gets-your-vote-for-mighty-drive-to-p3-in-monaco.4OALiqRbQW3MCAP22BCw7Q.html|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Formula 1]]|language=en|archive-date=28 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528165142/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.driver-of-the-day-ocon-gets-your-vote-for-mighty-drive-to-p3-in-monaco.4OALiqRbQW3MCAP22BCw7Q.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Delighted Ocon 'on a cloud' as Alpine claim first podium since 2021 in Monaco|date=28 May 2023|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.delighted-ocon-on-a-cloud-as-alpine-claim-first-podium-since-2021-in-monaco.6YzMdBNx2FkwQg5MxStxmt.html|access-date=29 May 2023|website=[[Formula 1]]|language=en|archive-date=28 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528210636/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.delighted-ocon-on-a-cloud-as-alpine-claim-first-podium-since-2021-in-monaco.6YzMdBNx2FkwQg5MxStxmt.html|url-status=live}}</ref> More points came at the [[2023 Spanish Grand Prix|Spanish]] and [[2023 Canadian Grand Prix|Canadian]] Grands Prix and in the rain-affected {{F1 GP|2023|Austrian}} sprint race where he held off Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and McLaren's [[Lando Norris]]. In the main race, Ocon received a record five time penalties for track limits violations and an unsafe pit box release.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Verstappen makes it five wins in a row with Austria victory |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.verstappen-beats-leclerc-for-victory-in-austria-to-make-it-five-wins-in-a.40RQJjhwhd2nethv4qEsyJ.html |access-date=6 July 2023 |website=www.formula1.com |language=en |archive-date=3 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703060619/https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.verstappen-beats-leclerc-for-victory-in-austria-to-make-it-five-wins-in-a.40RQJjhwhd2nethv4qEsyJ.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://racingnews365.com/ocon-sets-dubious-f1-record-in-austria|title=Ocon sets dubious F1 record in Austria|website=racingnews365.com|first1=Michael|last1=Butterworth|first2=Aaron|last2=Deckers|date=3 July 2023|accessdate=3 July 2023|archive-date=3 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703175317/https://racingnews365.com/ocon-sets-dubious-f1-record-in-austria|url-status=live}}</ref> Consecutive retirements followed with a hydraulics leak at the {{F1 GP|2023|British}} and a first-lap crash at the {{F1 GP|2023|Hungarian}}. He improved from fourteenth on the grid at the {{F1 GP|2023|Belgian}} to score points in eighth place.

Ocon retired from the {{F1 GP|2023|Italian}} "for safety reasons" due to a steering issue.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://racingnews365.com/ocon-explains-safety-issues-that-caused-monza-retirement|title=Ocon explains safety issues that caused Monza retirement|website=racingnews365.com|first1=Rory|last1=Mitchell|first2=Aaron|last2=Deckers|date=5 September 2023|accessdate=8 February 2024}}</ref> He then retired from sixth place at the {{F1 GP|2023|Singapore}} with a gearbox problem, his fourth non-finish in six races.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.not-the-best-birthday-says-race-retiree-ocon-as-gasly-comes-home-p6-after.7ix1yIuDsHM6o5mGOs02TX.html|title='Not the best birthday' says race retiree Ocon, as Gasly comes home P6 after 'intense' Singapore Grand Prix|website=formula1.com|date=18 September 2023|accessdate=8 February 2024}}</ref> He finished the {{F1 GP|2023|Qatar}} in seventh despite the hot weather conditions causing him to vomit into his helmet.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.crash.net/f1/news/1037757/1/ocon-was-throwing-cockpit-after-15-laps-due-intense-qatar-heat|title=Ocon was 'throwing up' in cockpit after 15 laps due to intense Qatar heat|website=crash.net|first=Lewis|last=Larkam|date=8 October 2023|accessdate=8 February 2024}}</ref> His seventh retirement of the season came at the {{F1 GP|2023|United States}} after a collision with [[Oscar Piastri]]. Ocon started sixteenth at the inaugural {{F1 GP|2023|Las Vegas}}, avoided collisions to improve to eighth on the first lap and climbed to fourth place by the end of the race.

Ocon ended the season twelfth in the World Drivers' Championship with 58 points compared to 62 for teammate Gasly, who qualified ahead of Ocon at fourteen of the twenty-two races.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.crash.net/f1/feature/1042253/1/f1-2023-headtoheads-which-drivers-dominated-their-teammates|title=F1 2023 head-to-heads: Which drivers dominated their teammates?|website=crash.net|date=27 November 2023|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> Ocon described the season as a "wasted opportunity" due to his high number of race retirements.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/ocon-switches-to-war-mode-after-wasted-opportunity-in-f1-2023/10555503/|title=Ocon switches to "war mode" after "wasted opportunity in F1 2023|website=motorsport.com|date=7 December 2023|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> [[Mark Hughes (journalist)|Mark Hughes]] at ''The Race'' commented that Ocon "did a pretty solid job" in 2023, but that as the season went on, "the momentum was with Gasly".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/every-2023-f1-driver-ranked-worst-best/|title=Every 2023 F1 driver ranked from worst to best|website=the-race.com|date=7 December 2023|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref>

==== 2024: Early departure ====
[[File:Esteban Ocon 2024 Chinese GP.jpg|thumb|left|Ocon at the [[2024 Chinese Grand Prix]]]]
Ocon continued alongside Gasly at Alpine for {{F1|2024}}. During pre-season testing, he noted that the team were "on the back foot".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.alpine-drivers-admit-team-on-the-back-foot-heading-into-2024.3ZeFMgcILBn1aSGZ7Bi60C.html|title=Alpine drivers admit team 'on the back foot' heading into 2024|website=formula1.com|date=27 February 2024|accessdate=16 March 2024}}</ref> The Alpine drivers qualified nineteenth and twentieth for the season-opening {{F1 GP|2024|Bahrain}}, which Gasly described as "not a surprise".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article.we-have-a-lot-of-work-ahead-of-us-alpine-drivers-say-double-q1-exit-not-a.5EFWYAdo9eZoruH8TDlaPA.html|title='We have a lot of work ahead of us' – Alpine drivers say double-Q1 exit 'not a surprise' in Bahrain|website=formula1.com|date=1 March 2024|accessdate=16 March 2024}}</ref> Ocon reached the second qualifying session at the {{F1 GP|2024|Australian}} but failed to make progress in the race. A helmet visor tear-off strip had got stuck in his car's brake duct, which Ocon believed had cost him a potential top-ten finish.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/ocon-visor-tear-off-cost-likely-points-finish-alpine-f1-team/10591926/|title=Ocon: Visor tear-off cost likely points finish to Alpine F1 team|website=motorsport.com|date=26 March 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> Ocon claimed the team's first points of 2024 at the {{F1 GP|2024|Miami}}, improving from thirteenth on the grid to tenth at the finish. He qualified eleventh at the {{F1 GP|2024|Monaco}} but retired after colliding with Gasly on track, for which he apologised and claimed responsibility.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/alpine-not-ruling-out-f1-driver-line-up-change-after-latest-ocon-gasly-clash/10616647/|title=Alpine not ruling out F1 driver line-up change after latest Ocon/Gasly clash|website=motorsport.com|first=Jonathan|last=Noble|date=27 May 2024|accessdate=28 May 2024}}</ref>

During the {{F1 GP|2024|Canadian}}, Alpine imposed [[team orders]] forcing Ocon to give up ninth place to Gasly, who was in better position to attack Daniel Ricciardo. However, after Gasly failed to pass Ricciardo, Alpine did not ask Gasly to give the place back to Ocon, a decision he described as "nonsense".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ocon unhappy with Alpine team orders in Canada |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/ocon-unhappy-with-nonsense-team-orders-in-canada-despite-double-points.74r9MgUW4haFOumwFOZBb1 |access-date=4 November 2024 |website=Formula 1® - The Official F1® Website |language=en}}</ref> Ocon reached the third qualifying session (Q3) for the first time in 2024 at the {{F1 GP|2024|Spanish}} and achieved another tenth-place finish.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/what-the-teams-said-race-day-in-spain-2024.49xI3oP6SPp3HeZo3GBIa5|title=What the teams said – Race day in Spain|website=formula1.com|date=23 June 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> Further Q3 appearances came at the [[2024 Austrian Grand Prix|Austrian]] and [[2024 Belgian Grand Prix|Belgian]] Grands Prix,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2024/races/1239/austria/qualifying|title=Formula 1 Qatar Airways Austrian Grand Prix 2024 - Qualifying|date=29 June 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/results/2024/races/1242/belgium/qualifying|title=Formula 1 Rolex Belgian Grand Prix 2024 - Qualifying|date=27 July 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> with Ocon scoring points in ninth place at the latter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/winners-losers-f1-2024-belgian-grand-prix/|title=Winners and losers from F1's 2024 Belgian Grand Prix|website=the-race.com|date=28 July 2026|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> He failed to score points at the following six races, but did set his first [[fastest lap]] at the {{F1 GP|2024|United States}} after Alpine brought him in for a late pit stop to deny Constructors' Championship rivals Williams the bonus point for fastest lap.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/ocon-sorry-for-colapinto-after-robbing-williams-driver-of-fastest-lap-point-at-us-gp/10665464/|title=Ocon "sorry" for Colapinto after robbing him of US GP fastest lap point|website=autosport.com|date=23 October 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref>

A qualifying session beset by rain and [[Racing flags#Red flag|red flags]] at the {{F1 GP|2024|São Paulo}} helped Ocon qualify in fourth place. He led part of the race after the drivers ahead pitted, but was ultimately overtaken by eventual race winner Max Verstappen. Ocon finished the race in second place ahead of Gasly in third, marking Alpine's first double-podium and the first for Team Enstone since 2013. This result more than tripled the team's points tally and promoted them from ninth to sixth in the World Constructors' Championship.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alpine pair overjoyed by unexpected double podium in Brazil |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/we-never-gave-up-and-here-we-are-alpine-pair-overjoyed-by-unexpected-double.62mmKviVydA0WmbOHp1zpc |access-date=4 November 2024 |website=Formula 1® - The Official F1® Website |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/the-uplifting-chapter-ocon-and-gasly-added-to-their-complicated-history/10670760/|title=The uplifting chapter Ocon and Gasly added to their complicated history|website=motorsport.com|date=5 November 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> Ocon was eliminated in a lap-one collision at the {{F1 GP|2024|Qatar}}, his final race for Alpine.

In June, shortly after his Monaco Grand Prix collision with Gasly, Alpine announced that Ocon would leave the team at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barretto |first=Lawrence |date=3 June 2024 |title=Alpine to part ways with Ocon at end of 2024 season |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/breaking-alpine-announce-they-will-part-ways-with-ocon-at-end-of-2024-season.7ra4uaXdrYOHfklwU9TEqH |access-date=3 June 2024 |website=Formula1.com |publisher=[[Formula One Administration]] |language=en}}</ref> In July, it was announced that he would join [[Haas F1 Team|Haas]] for the {{F1|2025}} season on a multi-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/breaking-haas-confirm-signing-of-ocon-with-frenchman-to-partner-bearman-in.7uQGY6qNKCZmU8fXM57TBi|title=Haas confirm signing of Ocon with Frenchman to partner Bearman in 2025|date=25 July 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> Ocon did not take part in the season-ending {{F1GP|2024|Abu Dhabi}}; his seat was taken by Alpine reserve driver [[Jack Doohan]], who was already set to replace Ocon in 2025.<ref name="AD24">{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/13264472/esteban-ocon-to-make-early-alpine-exit-as-jack-doohan-gets-to-start-f1-career-at-abu-dhabi-gp|title=Esteban Ocon to make early Alpine exit as Jack Doohan gets to start F1 career at Abu Dhabi GP|date=1 December 2024|access-date=1 December 2024}}</ref> It was reported that, since Ocon was under contract until the end of the year, Alpine required him to leave the team one race early in exchange for being allowed to drive for Haas at the post-season test.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/alpine-ultimatum-over-haas-test-forced-esteban-ocon-to-miss-f1-finale/|title=Ocon had to give up final Alpine race to ensure Haas test|website=the-race.com|date=1 December 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> Addressing speculation about the early driver change, Alpine team principal [[Oliver Oakes]] commented "I think it suits everybody".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/lets-see-oakes-expands-on-discussions-amid-reports-ocon-could-be-replaced-by.3yXxy4inZryhRzNkZBXKwf|title="Let's see" – Oakes expands on "discussions" amid reports Ocon could be replaced by Doohan for Abu Dhabi GP|website=formula1.com|date=1 December 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> In a message on [[Instagram]], Ocon thanked the team and wrote that "this is not how I wanted things to end."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ocon shares emotional farewell to Alpine |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/this-is-not-how-i-wanted-things-to-end-ocon-shares-emotional-farewell-to.XUOx2kM5WjY99EU8tdOdw |access-date=3 December 2024 |website=Formula 1® - The Official F1® Website |language=en}}</ref>

Ocon placed fourteenth in the World Drivers' Championship, scoring 23 points to Gasly's 36 up to and including the Qatar Grand Prix. The two drivers were fairly evenly-matched in head-to-head results, with Ocon qualifying ahead of Gasly at twelve of the twenty-three races.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/13274967/f1-final-2024-team-mate-qualifying-and-race-head-to-head-scores-featuring-lewis-hamilton-vs-george-russell-and-more|title=F1: Final 2024 team-mate qualifying and race head-to-head scores featuring Lewis Hamilton vs George Russell and more|website=skysports.com|date=31 December 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> Writers at ''Sky Sports'' praised Ocon's São Paulo performance but described his final season at Alpine as "otherwise a forgettable campaign".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/13270873/f1-driver-ratings-2024-ranking-this-seasons-grid-featuring-max-verstappen-lando-norris-lewis-hamilton-sergio-perez-and-more|title=F1 driver ratings 2024: Ranking this season's grid featuring Max Verstappen, Lando Norris, Lewis Hamilton, Sergio Perez and more|website=skysports.com|date=12 December 2024|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref>

=== Haas (2025–2026) ===

[[File:2025 Japan GP - Haas - Esteban Ocon - FP2.jpg|thumb|right|Ocon (pictured at the {{F1GP|2025|Japanese}}) signed for [[Haas F1 Team|Haas]] in {{F1|2025}}.|alt=Ocon driving the Haas VF-25 at the 2025 Japanese Grand Prix]]
Ocon joined Haas on a multi-year deal for 2025, partnering rookie [[Oliver Bearman]].<ref name="contract">{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/articles/cv2gzp0v0z7o |title=Haas sign Alpine's Ocon for 2025 season |date=25 July 2024 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |publisher=[[BBC]] |access-date=22 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240829182841/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/articles/cv2gzp0v0z7o |archive-date=29 August 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref> Ocon and Bearman qualified in the bottom two positions and finished last of the remaining drivers at the season-opening {{F1GP|2025|Australian}},<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/inside-the-aero-problems-that-will-keep-haas-near-the-back-of-the-f1-field/10705192/ |title=Inside the aero problems that will keep Haas near the back of the F1 field |last1=Boxall-Legge

2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> a result Ocon described as "unexpected".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/esteban-ocon-on-haas-performance-quite-unexpected-to-be-where-we-are/10704764/|title=Esteban Ocon on Haas performance: "Quite unexpected to be where we are"|website=motorsport.com|date=19 March 2025|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> He finished fifth from eighteenth on the grid at the {{F1GP|2025|Chinese}} following disqualifications for both [[Scuderia Ferrari|Ferrari]] drivers, achieving his first points finish in the [[Haas VF-25|VF-25]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.autosport.com/f1/news/leclerc-hamilton-and-gasly-disqualified-from-chinese-gp/10706422/ |title=Leclerc, Hamilton and Gasly disqualified from Chinese GP |last=Cleeren |first=Filip |archive-date=15 April 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> He retired with an engine failure at the {{F1 GP|2025|Emilia-Romagna}} but then scored further points at the [[2025 Monaco Grand Prix|Monaco]], [[2025 Canadian Grand Prix|Canadian]] and [[2025 Austrian Grand Prix|Austrian]] Grands Prix.

Ocon qualified and finished fifth at the {{F1 GP|2025|Belgian}} sprint, scoring a further four points, but failed to score in the main race, describing the team's tyre strategy as "frustrating".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/esteban-ocon-slams-big-and-costly-mistake-in-haas-spa-strategy/10746291/|title=Esteban Ocon slams "frustrating" mistakes that cost Haas in Belgian GP|website=motorsport.com|date=31 July 2025|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> He achieved more points finishes at the [[2025 Dutch Grand Prix|Dutch]], [[2025 Mexico City Grand Prix|Mexico City]] and [[2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix|Las Vegas]] Grands Prix, but was disqualified from qualifying at the {{F1 GP|2025|Azerbaijan}} for a technical infringement and was eliminated from the {{F1 GP|2025|United States}} sprint after a crash with Lance Stroll. He ended the season by qualifying in the top ten for the {{F1 GP|2025|Abu Dhabi}} and finishing seventh, although he described his car as unstable and having been "unmanageable for many races".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/f1-2025-recap-esteban-ocon-real-challenge-rookie-haas/10785767/|title=F1 2025 recap: Esteban Ocon got a real challenge from a rookie at Haas|website=motorsport.com|date=23 December 2025|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref>

Ocon finished fifteenth in the World Drivers' Championship with 38 points compared to 41 for teammate Bearman. Ocon was outqualified by Bearman at fourteen of the twenty-four races.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/13339705/f1-team-mate-head-to-head-qualifying-race-sprint-latest-scores-results-from-2025-season|title=F1 team-mate 2025 head-to-head: Qualifying, Race, Sprint latest scores, results from Formula 1 season|website=skysports.com|date=9 December 2025|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> Writers at ''The Race'' commented that Bearman's qualifying performance had "made life difficult" for Ocon,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the-race.com/formula-1/every-2025-f1-driver-ranked-from-worst-to-best/|title=Every 2025 F1 driver ranked from worst to best|website=the-race.com|date=13 December 2025|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref> and Haas team principal [[Ayao Komatsu]] remarked that the team had "expected more" from him.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/we-expected-more-from-esteban-ocon-haas/10795161/|title="We expected more" from Esteban Ocon – Haas|website=motorsport.com|date=7 February 2026|accessdate=30 September 2026}}</ref>

==== 2026: Second early departure ====
[[File:2026 Chinese GP - Haas - Esteban Ocon - Qualifying.jpg|left|thumb|Ocon driving at the [[2026 Chinese Grand Prix]]]]
Ocon continued driving alongside Bearman at Haas in {{F1|2026}}.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-25 |title=Esteban Ocon signs for Haas for 2025 F1 season |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/articles/cv2gzp0v0z7o |access-date=2026-09-04 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> At pre-season testing, Ocon stated that the [[Haas VF-26|VF-26]] had "good grip and balance", but had a challenge adapting to the new regulations, particularly in both energy management and engine deployment.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sree |first=Meghana |date=2026-02-24 |title=Haas 2026 Preview: Confident contenders for the 'best of the rest' title |url=https://www.dive-bomb.com/article/haas-2026-preview-confident-contenders-for-the-best-of-the-rest-title |access-date=2026-09-04 |website=DIVEBOMB Motorsport |language=en}}</ref>

Ocon qualified and finished outside the top ten at the first two races (the [[2026 Australian Grand Prix|Australian]] and [[2026 Chinese Grand Prix|Chinese]] Grands Prix) whilst Bearman scored a total of 17 points.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Points in Australia were 'a boost' for Haas – Bearman |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/weve-got-to-keep-it-up-now-bearman-says-points-in-australia-were-what-haas.294NHj2N9dsXeyeu7QvuKV |access-date=2026-09-04 |website=Formula1.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=15 March 2026 |title=Bearman overjoyed by P5 finish in China after 'deer in the headlights' scare with Hadjar |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/bearman-overjoyed-by-p5-finish-in-china-after-deer-in-the-headlights-scare.2Q5gywHm3hxtqzxWYJoskJ |access-date=23 March 2026 |website=Formula1.com |language=en}}</ref> Ocon was given a ten-second time penalty at the latter for colliding with [[Franco Colapinto]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/esteban-ocon-apologises-to-franco-colapinto-after-chinese-gp-collision/10805761/|title=Fans told 'don't send death threats' as Esteban Ocon apologises for Franco Colapinto clash|website=Motorsport.com|date=16 March 2026|access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> Ocon scored a point at the {{F1 GP|2026|Japanese}}, finishing tenth, having been disadvantaged by the timing of a safety car.<ref>{{Cite web |title=P10 Ocon laments timing of the Safety Car at Suzuka |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/video/p10-ocon-laments-timing-of-the-safety-car-at-suzuka.1860979472759980354 |access-date=2026-09-04 |website=Formula1.com |language=en}}</ref> Further points came at the {{F1 GP|2026|Monaco}}, where he improved from seventeenth on the grid to ninth at the finish. After another elimination in the first qualifying session (Q1) at the {{F1 GP|2026|Belgian}}, Ocon claimed that "only [Bearman's] car works as it should", complaining of a lack of straight-line speed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/eliminated-in-q1-again-ocon-resigned-the-car-thats-performing-normally-is-ollies/10839961/|title='Only Oliver Bearman's car works as it should' – Esteban Ocon explains another Q1 knockout|website=Motorsport.com|date=19 July 2026|access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref> Ocon and Bearman collided on the first lap of the race, causing tyre punctures for both cars.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/ocon-bearman-contact-this-must-never-happen-again-full-stop/10841307/|title=Esteban Ocon and Oliver Bearman contact 'cannot happen again, full stop'|website=Motorsport.com|date=24 July 2026|access-date=30 September 2026}}</ref>

Ocon retired from the {{F1 GP|2026|Dutch}} with an engine failure. He started the {{F1 GP|2026|Azerbaijan}} in thirteenth place and improved to eighth at the finish, his best result of the season thus far. After the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in September, Ocon confirmed that he would leave Haas at the end of the season. Writing on social media, Ocon said he was proud of his performances "in what were not always the easiest of circumstances" and that his departure was "absolutely not the end" of his Formula One career.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-30 |title=Esteban Ocon: Haas driver to leave team at end of 2026 F1 season after two years with American-owned squad |url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/13593556/esteban-ocon-haas-driver-to-leave-team-at-end-of-2026-f1-season-after-two-years-with-american-owned-squad |access-date=2026-09-30 |website=[[Sky Sports]] |language=en}}</ref> At the {{F1 GP|2026|Mexico City}}, Ocon was replaced by reserve driver [[Ryo Hirakawa]] for the first practice session (FP1) as part of the requirement for all teams to run rookie drivers in a select number of these sessions. Ocon returned to his seat for FP2, during which there was a dispute between Ocon and his race engineer regarding tyre choice.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benson |first=Andrew |date=2026-10-31 |title=Mexico City Grand Prix: Esteban Ocon denies reports of physical altercation behind Haas dropping |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/formula1/articles/c3n04vjjpkv4o |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Prior to FP3 on the day before the race, Haas announced that Hirakawa would replace Ocon for the remainder of the weekend. No reason was given for the change.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/hirakawa-to-replace-ocon-at-haas-for-remainder-of-mexico-city-grand-prix-weekend.2cl5jN0g3rZ2pIYQvc00xM|title=Hirakawa to replace Ocon at Haas for remainder of Mexico City Grand Prix weekend|website=Formula1.com|date=31 October 2026|access-date=31 October 2026}}</ref> 

Two days after the Mexico City Grand Prix, Haas announced that Ocon would be released from the team with immediate effect and would be replaced by [[FIA Formula 2 Championship|Formula 2]] championship leader [[Rafael Câmara]], who was already set to replace Ocon for the {{F1|2027}} season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Camara to make F1 debut for Haas in Sao Paulo |url=https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/f2-racer-camara-to-make-f1-debut-at-sao-paulo-grand-prix-as-haas-confirm-ocon-will-not-return.12Qa0tpaMZ9kgnEuGJBKFp |access-date=2026-11-03 |website=www.formula1.com |language=en}}</ref> In a statement, team principal Komatsu said that the decision was "in the best interest of the team" and that the conversations between the team and Ocon that led to his dismissal were an "internal matter".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/articles/ck054q3g5jnpo|title=Ocon dropped by Haas for rest of season after row|website=bbc.co.uk|date=3 November 2026|accessdate=3 November 2026}}</ref>
